title: Can you put it in a sponsored video?
instruction: The school video will run on YouTube and at the end it shows the logo of a local company that paid for it. That is commercial use. Decide about each piece.
buckets: Allowed, just credit the author (or not even that)
Allowed, but then the whole video must have the CC BY-SA licence

items.text: A photo of a castle from Wikimedia Commons with the CC BY licence
items.why: CC BY allows anything, even commercial use, as long as you credit the author, the licence and a link to the source.

items.text: Music with the CC BY-SA licence as background for the whole video
items.why: Under CC, music combined with a picture is an adaptation of the work. SA means “share alike”: your video must get the same licence.

items.text: A track with the CC BY-NC licence
items.why: NC forbids commercial use. The sponsor pays for showing its logo, so the video is commercial.

items.text: An illustration with the CC BY-ND licence that you draw the school logo into
items.why: ND forbids changes. An added logo is a change, even if it is small.

items.text: A shot from the film Sprite Fright, (CC) Blender Foundation, licence CC BY
items.why: Blender Studio’s open films are CC BY. Just credit “(CC) Blender Foundation | studio.blender.org”.

items.text: A sound of applause with the CC0 licence
items.why: CC0 means the author has given up their rights. You don’t have to credit them, but it is polite.

items.text: A picture from a search engine that has no licence at all
items.why: Without a licence, “all rights reserved” applies. Being on the internet does not make a picture free.

items.text: A picture from an AI generator showing an almost exact copy of a famous cartoon character
items.why: The generator’s terms may “give” you the output, but the character belongs to the studio. The generator cannot hand out rights to it.

debrief: Creative Commons licences are a kit of four parts: BY (credit the author), SA (share alike), NC (non-commercial only), ND (no changes). CC0 is completely free. When there is no licence, you may do almost nothing. And AI output is not automatically free: check what is in it.
